To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the genetic interaction between mitochondrial function and schizophrenia may reveal by DRD2-linked NDUFS7 via protein-protein interactions between FLNA and ARBB2 and the biological mechanism of signaling pathways for coagulation cascade may be revealed by the PPI of the SCZ candidate genes and the coagulant-associated genes.
the genetic interaction of mitochondria dysfunction and the hemostatic pathway may play an important role in the pathophysiology of schizophrenia.

the genetic interaction between mitochondrial function and schizophrenia is modulated by DRD2 and the biological mechanism of signaling pathways of coagulation is illustrated by the PIPPI network of the candidate genes and the coagulopathy-associated genes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the genetic interactions of mitochondrial function and coagulation pathway in schizophrenia.
the genetic and biological mechanism of energy metabolism, coagulation function, and schizophrenia.
the biological mechanisms of schizophrenia and antithrombotic treatment of antipsychotics.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
schizophrenia is a multifaceted disease and the pathogenicity of this disorder is a complex interaction between genetic and environmental factors.
the biological functions of mitochondria and hemostasis may have important roles in disease pathology of schizophrenia.
schizophrenia may be a disease caused by the dysregulation of mitochondria and coagulation functions in brain tissues.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the genetic interaction of SCZMN and its associated genes may give rise to the biological dysfunction of mitochondrial function and the hemostatic process of schizophrenia.
the mitochondrial dysfunction and hemostatic pathway are the potential biological pathways for the negative and withdraw symptoms and antipsychotics-induced venous thrombosis of schizophrenia.
the genetic interaction of SCZCG and mitochondria function may be the potential pathogenic mechanism of energy metabolism in schizophrenia.
The main takeaway from our work is that

schizophrenia may be a complex disorder with multiple pathogenic pathways and the genetic interaction between mitochondrial dysfunction and coagulation cascade may be a potential target for treatment of negative and withdraw symptoms in schizophrenia.
the genetic interaction of SCZCG and coagulation factors may provide new clues to explain the biological mechanism for antipsychotic induced venous thrombo embolism (VTE).

the co-expressed candidate genes and reached candidate pathways in the SCZMN may be the key to understanding the biological mechanisms responsible of the negative and withdraw symptoms in schizophrenia and antipsycotic-induced venous tromboembolism.
